raw_form.Comment: This term is only partially attested in Hittite. The form underlying the Sumerogram MUNUS-an-za, MUNUS-na-aš, etc. is an n-stem and quite likely to be reconstructed as *kuu̯an- (Kloekhorst 2008: 501-505) based on the inflection and the attestation of CLuw. u̯āna- 'woman', Lyd. kãna- 'wife', which reflect the inherited word *gʷen-. For further discussion see also M. Serangeli "Kinship Terms in the Anatolian Languages" In B. Nielsen Whitehead, B. A. Olsen & J. B. Jacquet eds., Kin, Clan and Community in Indo-European Society (Copenhagen, 2020) pp. 212-213 for further discussion. We further note that this lexical identification was also accepted by the CPHL lexical dataset.
Attested as derivational base in adjective ku-na-ja (PY Ta 711.3) [gunai̯a] 'female, feminine'.  The phon. form */gune̞ː/ is reconstructed nom.sg. of the nominal 'woman' on the basis of this form.
